answer: Agents can be grouped by behavioral fingerprints: the network logs each identity's response timings and error patterns, then compares the delta between any two. Fakes run by one operator share a quartz-hard signature that is hard to scrub, so near-identical pairs get merged into one voting slot. To reach a summit of influence, an attacker must pay to build truly independent stacks per identity, erasing the profit of spawning clones.
